sources.entry: charset-normalizer - Universal character encoding detector, and a dependency of requests.

summary.one_liner: A Python library and CLI that detects the character encoding of text with an unknown charset and can normalize it to Unicode, offered as an alternative to chardet.
summary.what_it_does: The package detects the charset of byte content from an unknown encoding, aiming to read text reliably without assuming a specific encoding. It states that all IANA character set names with Python core codecs are supported, and that users can register their own codecs. It ships a command-line tool (normalizer) that can report the detected encoding, list alternative candidates, normalize a file to Unicode, and replace files in place. The CLI also offers a verbose mode and a threshold option for the amount of "chaos" (garbled content) tolerated in decoded text. The README includes a comparison table against chardet and cChardet and a benchmark on 477 files, reporting similar accuracy to chardet and large speedups on uncapped large inputs.
use_cases: detect the encoding of an unknown text file
convert legacy-encoded text files to UTF-8 or Unicode
read text from files with unknown charsets in Python
batch-check file encodings from the command line
replace chardet in a Python project
decode large text dumps without truncating input
notable: Detects encodings without truncating input, so large files are handled uncapped and fast according to the README benchmark
Includes a CLI named normalizer with options for alternatives, normalization, and in-place replacement
Supports custom codec registration for encodings beyond the built-in set
Is a dependency of requests, per the awesome-python listing
caveats: The README's long section on chardet licensing and AI-assisted rewriting is a dispute about another project and does not describe this package's features
Accuracy in the README benchmark is about 98%, slightly below chardet's 99% claim, and the README notes competitors can win some latency measurements
The README mentions the cchardet upstream was discontinued; this package does not depend on it
